subject: Order Form + MSA: clarification on term, auto-renew, and termination-for-convenience
messages:
From: Jillian Park <jillian.park@acmeanalytics.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acmeanalytics.com>; Acme Legal <legal@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form redlines + questions on term/notice/exit

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week — team liked the latency numbers. Attached are our annotated redlines on the Order Form and a short list of questions we need aligned before we can issue a PO. High level asks:

- Term length: we flagged the default 12-month term and asked for clarity on renewal cadence; would prefer 12-month with annual auto-renew unless either party provides notice.
- Auto-renew notice window: can Redwood accept 60 days notice rather than 90? Our procurement window is tight for Q4 budgeting.
- Termination for convenience (TFC): Acme prefers a 30-day TFC with refund of unused prepaid amounts for committed annual prepay pilots.
- Data retention/export: need to confirm export window after termination (minimum 30 days).

We attached ACME_OrderForm_redlines_20260719.pdf (comments inline). Can you confirm what positions Redwood will take and whether legal needs to redline the MSA? Happy to hop on a 30-min call to close.

Thanks,

Jillian Park
Head of Procurement | Acme Analytics
Jillian.Park@acmeanalytics.com
(415) 555-0198

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Order form redlines + questions on term/notice/exit

Jillian — thanks for the clear redlines and the call request. Looping in Laura (legal) and Ben (commercial/legal) to confirm positions.

Quick internal thoughts:
- Term/renewal: we typically do 12-months with automatic 12-month renewals unless notice provided. We can be flexible on the notice window for enterprise deals.
- Notice: 60 days is within the realm of possibility for larger customers; we need legal signoff on language to ensure it’s mutual.
- TFC: not something we give broadly without scope limits; Ben/Laura, can you propose a capped TFC exposure (e.g., N days of fees or remaining prepaid balance) and a data transition commitment?

Proposed next steps:
1) Ben/Laura to send proposed clause language we can share back with Jillian by EOD tomorrow.
2) If Acme is ok with the proposed compromise, schedule a 30-min commercial + legal wrap-up (I’m available Wed/Thu).

Cc’ing both so we can keep this in a single thread.

Cheers,
Dylan

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 15:26:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Order form redlines + questions on term/notice/exit (proposed legal positions)

Folks — drafted legal positions below (high-level; will convert to tracked redline if we agree):

1) Term and Auto-renew
   - Keep the 12-month initial term.
   - Auto-renew: mutual automatic 12-month renewals unless either party provides written notice not less than sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term. (Redwood is willing to accept 60 days for this customer class.)

2) Notice Window
   - Make the notice mutual (both parties can opt out with the same window).

3) Termination for Convenience (TFC)
   - Redwood is open to a limited TFC for this enterprise pilot only. Proposed compromise: Acme may terminate for convenience with sixty (60) days prior written notice; Redwood's liability for TFC shall be limited to (a) the unused portion of any prepaid fees on a pro rata basis, or (b) if no prepaid fees, a termination fee equal to thirty (30) days of average monthly recurring fees, at Acme's election.
   - No other consequential or indirect damages; standard mutual limitation of liability applies.

4) Data retention/export
   - Default data retention after termination: Redwood will retain account data for thirty (30) days after termination to allow export. For Enterprise customers, offer an extended 90-day transition window (export assistance available).

5) Transition assistance
   - Redwood will provide reasonable transition assistance as a one-time flat fee or swap into professional services (TBD), not to exceed agreed-upon TCV-based cap.

I can prepare a tracked redline of the Order Form and MSA (limited to the above sections) and share via Drive/DocuSign if you want to move fast. Recommend we present the compromise to Acme as a single bundle: 60-day mutual notice + limited TFC (60-day notice and capped refund/30-day fee) + 30-day default export / 90-day enterprise transition.

Ben Carter
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0BzAcme/OrderForm-v3 (I'll upload the tracked redline there by EOD)

From: Jillian Park <jillian.park@acmeanalytics.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acmeanalytics.com>; Acme Legal <legal@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form redlines + questions on term/notice/exit

Dylan / Ben / Laura — thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed language. A couple of clarifications from Acme legal/procurement:

- The 60-day mutual notice is acceptable.
- On TFC: Acme still prefers a straight refund of unused prepay for annual prepay pilots instead of Redwood’s capped alternative; is Redwood willing to take the full prepaid refund for the pilot cohort only?
- On data retention: 30-day default is minimal for us. We need to ensure that exports are complete and support is available during that period. Would Redwood agree to a 60-day export window for pilots?

We can accept the bundle if Redwood will: (1) agree to full unused prepay refund for the pilot cohort; and (2) extend the default export window to 60 days for the pilot. If Redwood cannot accept #1, please confirm the monetary cap (Ben’s draft suggested 30 days of fees or unused prepaid — which one governs?).

If you can confirm items above, we can circulate a PO. If not, I suggest a 30-min alignment call tomorrow.

Best,
Jillian

Attachments: Acme_PO_Draft_20260721.pdf

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Jillian Park <jillian.park@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com; laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form redlines + questions on term/notice/exit — Redwood positions and next steps

Jillian — appreciate the clarity. Summarizing Redwood's final positions for the pilot (so you can share with Procurement/Legal):

1) Term & Auto-renew: 12-month initial term with automatic 12-month renewals unless either party gives sixty (60) days written notice prior to term end (mutual).

2) Notice Window: 60 days mutual — accepted.

3) Termination for Convenience (pilot cohort compromise): Redwood will accept termination for convenience for this pilot with sixty (60) days prior written notice; Redwood's financial exposure will be limited to the unused prepaid balance for customers who have paid upfront. For customers on monthly billing, Redwood will accept a termination fee equivalent to thirty (30) days of average monthly charges. In short: prepaid customers get a refund of unused prepay; monthly customers will receive 30-day fee equivalence. (Ben, please confirm the precise fallback language in the draft redline.)

4) Data retention/export: For pilot customers Redwood will extend the export window to sixty (60) days and provide reasonable export assistance during that window. For standard enterprise customers we keep the 90-day transition assistance offer as previously noted.

5) Transition assistance: Redwood will provide standard export tooling plus a single 4-hour assisted export session for the pilot (no additional charge); further professional services are available if needed.

Next steps:
- Ben to drop a tracked redline into the Drive folder and share a DocuSign-friendly order form by EOD Thu.
- Jillian to confirm acceptance and circulate the PO once redline readback matches.
- If any remaining points, schedule a 30-min call Friday to finalize.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Cheers,
Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Dylan.Brooks@redwood.com
